paragraphs.source_en: [reject] the details of religious and sectarian [teachings,] believing them to be manmade laws and embellished tricks. 100 Ghazali claimed to have nothing against mathematics and science. Indeed, in his later autobiography he gladly admitted that they were capable of producing useful results. But mathematics and Aristotle’s logic are totally irrelevant to revealed religion and matters of faith because in the end they refer only to themselves. If the philosophers had actually arrived at truth, why did the philosophers and scientists, both ancient and modern, so often disagree with one another? Regarding God, the best these sages could come up with was the notion of the First Cause or the Creator. But this hung God’s existence on nothing more substantial than the proposition that an infinite regression is impossible.

But this hung God’s existence on nothing more substantial than the proposition that an infinite regression is impossible.

paragraphs.source_en: And having fulfilled his function as First Cause, what was left for God to do thereafter? Such a philosophy has no place for God to know, see, or hear, or to have any knowledge of particulars. Yet the Quran explicitly stated (34. 3) that nothing escapes God’s knowledge, “not even the smallest particle in heaven or on earth.”101 Worse, some of these same experts then proceeded to argue that the world is eternal, with neither beginning nor end, in which case there was no need for God to have intervened in the first place.
